specification.problem: Reduce quantum cost (QC) of 4-bit reversible circuits by applying an existing tool that finds gate-count-optimal Toffoli networks for any 4-variable function, and compare QC against previously known circuits for benchmarks and published designs.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Classical reversible circuit synthesis/optimization on 4 bits; no quantum algorithm with measurement. Abstract gives no details of the tool or the QC procedure, so only the optimization objectives and the reported savings are reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: Gate count of a reversible circuit
Quantum cost of a reversible circuit
Relative QC saving versus previously known circuit

equations.label: GC minimization
equations.description: Exact minimization of gate count of a Toffoli network C realizing f; the tool solves this for 4 variables.
equations.abstract_quote: finding optimal gate count Toffoli networks for any 4variable function
equations.justification: Abstract states the tool finds optimal GC Toffoli networks for any 4-variable function.

equations.label: QC minimization goal
equations.description: Target objective: reduce quantum cost of circuits realizing f.
equations.abstract_quote: exact minimization of quantum cost (QC) in 4-bit circuits
equations.justification: Abstract names QC minimization in 4-bit circuits as the goal.

equations.label: Relative saving
equations.description: Relative QC saving versus previously known circuits; reported maximum about 74%.
equations.abstract_quote: savings in QC of up to 74% comparing with previously known circuits
equations.justification: Formalizes the stated percentage saving; the formula is the standard definition.

registers.name: x
registers.role: Four-bit reversible data lines carrying the input/output of f (classical bits)

specification.initial_state: Classical 4-bit input x in {0,1}^4; the circuit realizes the permutation f on all 16 basis states (no quantum superposition required).

steps.description: Take a 4-bit reversible function f from a benchmark or published design, with its previously known circuit and QC.
Apply the GC-optimal Toffoli network synthesis tool to f (or to 4-bit sub-blocks) to get a minimal-gate-count network.
Evaluate QC of the resulting network (and alternatives) under a QC model; keep the lowest-QC realization. The exact procedure is not given in the abstract.
Compare new QC with previously known QC to compute the saving.

specification.measurement: No quantum measurement. Evaluation is classical: verify the synthesized network reproduces f on all 16 input states, and compute GC and QC of the result.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute QC of each candidate network under a QC model, select the minimum, and compute the relative saving S against the previously known circuit's QC for each benchmark/design; report the maximum (up to 74%).
assumptions: Savings are the standard relative reduction in QC.
Step 3 assumes QC is evaluated per candidate network; the abstract does not specify how.
Circuit plan is a generic classical synthesis workflow, not a quantum circuit.
Functional verification on all 16 inputs is assumed as the check; the abstract does not state it.
Functional equivalence is checked by exhaustive evaluation on 16 inputs.
missing_information: How GC-optimal networks are converted or used to reduce QC
